wines.name: Marisa Cuomo Furore Bianco 2024
wines.sub: Costa d'Amalfi DOC Furore · Campania, Italy
wines.flag: Same estate as the Rosato on Oct 28. Furore Bianco is the white from Marisa Cuomo's home village, a step up from the basic Costa d'Amalfi Bianco and below the flagship Fiorduva. The 2024 won Gambero Rosso's Tre Bicchieri, its top award.
factors: Climate
Warm Mediterranean, but the vines hang on steep terraces from 100 to 750 m, with constant sea breezes and cool nights. Freshness survives the southern sun.
Soil
Limestone and dolomite rock, with thin soils carried up and walled onto terraces by hand: 'heroic' viticulture. Gives a salty, stony character.
Grapes
Falanghina (locally Biancazita): citrus, apple, white flowers, firm acidity. Biancolella (locally Biancatenera): floral, herbal, softer. The two are traditionally vinified together.
Winemaking
Fermented and kept in stainless steel, no oak. Bottled young to keep the fruit and saltiness.
Producer
Founded in 1980 by Andrea Ferraioli and Marisa Cuomo in Furore. Their work helped revive local grapes and shape the Costa d'Amalfi DOC.
wines.concl: Very good. Fresh acidity and ripe Mediterranean fruit in balance; saline, nutty length gives more interest than most coastal whites.
wines.say: The Amalfi Coast in a glass: lemon, white flowers and sea salt from cliffside terraces above the water.

wines.name: Domaine Laporte Sancerre Les Garennes 2025
facts: Les Garennes, single vineyard south of Sancerre village
wines.flag: "Terroir du Jurassique" and the fossil shells on the label point to the soil: Jurassic limestone formed from ancient seabeds, full of fossilised shells. Les Garennes grows on caillottes, the small limestone pebbles that give Sancerre its most fragrant style. Founded in 1850 in Saint-Satur, the estate has belonged to the Bourgeois family of Chavignol since 1986.
factors: Climate
Cool continental, far from the sea. Short, sometimes cool summers keep acidity high and alcohol moderate.
Soil

Sancerre has three soils: caillottes (stony limestone), terres blanches (Kimmeridgian marl) and silex (flint). Caillottes give the most aromatic, early-drinking wines; flint gives smokier, tighter ones.
Grape
Sauvignon Blanc: aromatic, high acid, with citrus, green apple, gooseberry and grassy or flinty notes. In the Loire it's leaner and more mineral than in New Zealand.
Winemaking
Fermented and aged in stainless steel to protect fresh aromas. No oak.
Producer
Laporte vinifies each soil separately: Le Rochoy on flint, La Comtesse on marl, Les Garennes on caillottes.
wines.concl: Very good. Pronounced, pure Sauvignon fruit balanced by high acidity and a chalky, mineral finish; clean and precise.
wines.say: Classic Sancerre from an organic single vineyard: grapefruit, gooseberry and chalk. The benchmark for Sauvignon Blanc.

wines.name: Tinto Amorio Monje Skin-Contact 2024
wines.flag: Not a red, and not from Tenerife. Tinto Amorio is the producer (a Healdsburg winery) and Monje is the cuvée. It's an amber or "orange" wine: white grapes fermented on their skins like a red. Serve it chilled. A slight haze is normal, since it's unfined and unfiltered.
factors: Grapes
Gewürztraminer: pink-skinned and intensely aromatic (lychee, rose, ginger), naturally low in acid. The 8% Zinfandel adds red-berry fruit and a little colour.
Winemaking
Nine days fermenting on the skins pulls colour, tannin and texture from them, as with a red wine. That's what makes it amber and gives it grip. Native yeast, no fining or filtering.
Climate
Grapes come from organic vineyards around California. Past vintages drew on Mendocino and San Luis Obispo, both cooler, coast-influenced areas that help Gewürztraminer keep some freshness.
Producer

Tinto Amorio is a small Healdsburg winery, founded by a group of friends, making low-intervention wines from organic grapes. The blend changes each year: earlier Monje vintages were based on French Colombard.
wines.concl: Good to very good. Pronounced aromatics and light tannic grip balance a softer acid frame; fun and characterful rather than complex.
wines.ready: Drink now. Not intended for ageing.
wines.say: A California orange wine: Gewürztraminer fermented on its skins, with lychee, rose and grapefruit, a bit of grip, and serve it chilled.

wines.name: Domaine d'Ardhuy Ladoix 2023
wines.sub: Ladoix AOC · Côte de Beaune, Burgundy, France
wines.flag: Ladoix is a hidden-value village. It sits at the northern tip of the Côte de Beaune, at the foot of the Corton hill, where the Côte de Beaune meets the Côte de Nuits. It's little known, so prices stay modest for village-level Burgundy. The domaine is based at Clos des Langres in Corgoloin, named on the label.
factors: Vintage

2023 was one of Burgundy's hottest years on record, with a very large crop. The risk for reds was dilution; the good ones are charming and juicy, with bright red fruit and light, fine tannins. Approachable young.
Site
East- and south-facing slopes below the famous Corton hill (Grand Cru). Limestone and marl soils.
Grape
Pinot Noir: thin-skinned, pale, high acid, low to medium tannin, red fruit; earth and forest floor as it ages.
Winemaking
Aged in oak barrels. Village Burgundy usually sees some new oak but stays fruit-led.
Producer
Family estate on the border of the Côte de Beaune and Côte de Nuits, passed from father to daughters. Holdings run from Ladoix and Corton to Clos de Vougeot.
wines.concl: Very good. Juicy red fruit, fresh acidity and fine tannin in balance; the generous 2023 style makes it open and charming now, with more structure than a regional Bourgogne.
wines.say: Village Burgundy from the foot of the Corton hill: cherry, raspberry and fine tannin, without the famous-name price.

lineup.sub: An Amalfi Coast white, an organic single-vineyard Sancerre, a California orange wine and village Burgundy from Ladoix.
